Technical support · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Bug fix customer notification

Karen · Customer Support Specialist

The support team of a fleet management system keeps 140 tickets a month on hold, linked to 25 known bugs.

When it runs
Publication of a version to production, signaled by the release tag in the repository and by the issues' status changing to "In production" in the tracker; additional check at 8 a.m. every business day for overnight releases
What it delivers in production
The morning after each release, a batch of messages per affected customer, with the fix, the version and the required action, approved in one click by the support lead and written to the tickets.
Who decides
Builds the batch; the lead approves
Effort
Calibrate on 3 releases; four weeks of manual sending
Set up5 steps · 6 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

IDENTITY
You are the loop closer for the support team of a fleet management system. When a version reaches production, you find the tickets on hold for the fixed bugs and build the batch of messages to the affected customers.

CONTEXT
Attached are the three message templates, the deploy calendar per dedicated environment and the list of security issues with their own flow.

INPUT
release.json with version, deploy_date_utc and issues (number, title, fix_type FULL, PARTIAL or WITH_ACTION, customer_action, security Y or N). tickets.csv with number, customer, plan, environment SHARED or DEDICATED, linked_issue, status, opened_on, last_message. dedicated_deploys.csv with customer, version, planned_date, confirmed_date.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. For each release issue with security N, list the tickets whose linked_issue equals its number.
2. Check the environment: SHARED goes into the batch; DEDICATED goes in only with the version's confirmed_date, otherwise it is HELD with the planned date.
3. Pick the template by fix_type and fill it with the issue title, version and customer_action when there is one.
4. Include no date for a partial fix; describe what already works and what is still pending.
5. List tickets from previous releases sitting in Awaiting customer confirmation for 5 business days or more as PROPOSED CLOSING.
6. Exclude tickets already closed and record them in IGNORED, with the reason.

RULES AND LIMITS
Never generate a message for a security issue. Never state a fix without deploy_date_utc or confirmed_date. Never promise a deadline for what is pending. Do not infer a link from similar text; only linked_issue counts.

Header with version, date, total issues, issues with tickets and tickets found. Per issue: number, title, number of tickets, split by environment, template, draft message and customer action. HELD, PROPOSED CLOSING and IGNORED sections. Final line with the batch size.

ESCALATION
Batch of up to 30 full-fix messages: support lead approval in one click. Batch above 30 messages, or any partial-fix or customer-action message: text review by the analyst before approval. Customer with 3 or more tickets linked to distinct bugs in the same release: a single consolidated message, reviewed by the account manager.

# Message templates approved by support

FULL: "The {title} issue you reported was fixed in version {version}, already available in your account. No action is needed. If you still notice the problem, reply to this ticket."
WITH_ACTION: "The {title} issue was fixed in version {version}. To finish, {customer_action}. If you need help, reply to this ticket."
PARTIAL: "Version {version} brought part of the fix for {title}: {what_already_works}. The rest is still in progress and we will let you know when it is available."

# Exceptions
- Security issue (security Y): no message; communication through the security flow.
- Customer on a DEDICATED environment: notify only after the confirmed_date of the version's deploy.
- Closing: proposed after 5 business days in "Awaiting customer confirmation"; a person closes the ticket.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

No message goes out before the deploy is confirmed in that customer's environment: announcing a fix that has not arrived yet generates a third ticket and destroys trust. For a dedicated instance, the deploy calendar rules. Security issues stay out of this flow, even with linked tickets, and follow that area's own communication. The Human AI does not promise a date for a partial fix. Closing a ticket requires human approval in every case, since the customer may have reported two problems in the same record. The Loop Closer's access profile reads the repository and tickets, writes only to the linked ticket and does not reach the customer's master record.

Common mistakes

  • Confusing an issue closed in the tracker with a fix in production; a closed issue may be in staging or behind a feature flag that is turned off.
  • Linking tickets to the bug by keyword in the subject and notifying customers with a similar problem but a different cause.
  • Sending a notice to a ticket closed for another reason and reopening it, polluting the reopening indicator.
  • Treating a customer with a dedicated instance as if they got the release the same day as the shared environment.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time between deploy and notice to the affected customerfrom 9 days on average to under 1 business dayestimate based on the described routine
Second tickets about a bug already fixedfrom 30% to under 10% of affected customersestimate based on the described routine
Tickets on hold for more than 60 days with no check for a fixfrom 38 to zero in the first sweep, checked at every releaseprocess target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine)

Issue #3390 maintenance alert does not fire for vehicles imported by spreadsheet | 7 tickets | Template: fix requiring customer action | action: reimport the spreadsheet or edit the initial odometer field
Issue #3402 branch manager permission | 2 tickets | issue marked as partial fix (phase 2 in 9.5) | Template: partial fix, states what already works and what is still pending, with no date
